record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: For Hénon maps H_{a,b} with (a,b) in WY, do any two distinct kneading sequences determine a unique parameter pair (a,b), and hence determine all other kneading sequences in K?

evidence.quote: Question 13. — Is it true that any two distinct kneading sequences of the Hénon map Ha,b, with (a, b) ∈ WY, determine a unique pair of parameters (a, b), and in that way govern all the other kneading sequences in K of Ha,b?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For real parameters $a$ and $b$, let $H_{a,b}\colon\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be the Hénon map $H_{a,b}(x,y)=(1-ax^2+y,\,bx)$. Let $\mathcal{WY}\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ denote the Wang–Young parameter set: a positive-measure set of strongly dissipative parameters $(a,b)$ (with $0<b\ll 1$ and $a$ near $2$) for which $H_{a,b}$ admits a topologically transitive strange attractor with a unique SRB measure and a positive Lyapunov exponent on a positive-measure set of points. For $(a,b)\in\mathcal{WY}$, kneading theory associates to $H_{a,b}$ a set $K(a,b)$ of kneading sequences, each sequence being an infinite symbolic itinerary that records the combinatorial behavior of orbits on the attractor (analogous to the Milnor–Thurston kneading invariants for unimodal interval maps).

Question: Is it true that for any two distinct kneading sequences $s_1, s_2 \in K(a,b)$, the pair $(s_1,s_2)$ uniquely determines the parameter pair $(a,b)\in\mathcal{WY}$, and consequently determines all the other kneading sequences in $K(a,b)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the recent compilation of open problems on Hénon maps. Related progress has classified Hénon maps on Wang–Young parameters up to conjugacy on the strange attractor by their full set of kneading sequences (equivalently, by folding patterns), but the sharper question of whether just two distinct kneading sequences suffice to determine the parameter pair, and hence all other kneading sequences, does not appear to be resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Question 13. Is it true that any two distinct kneading sequences of the Hénon map H_{a,b}, with (a,b) ∈ WY, determine a unique pair of parameters (a,b), and in that way govern all the other kneading sequences in K of H_{a,b}?
status_evidence.claim: The uniqueness-from-two-kneading-sequences question is stated as an open question.

status_evidence.title: The pruning front conjecture, folding patterns and classification of Hénon maps in the presence of strange attractors
status_evidence.snippet: Classification: two Hénon maps in WY are conjugate on their strange attractors iff their sets of kneading sequences coincide iff their folding patterns coincide.
status_evidence.claim: A classification using the full set of kneading sequences exists, but not using only two of them.
